title: Add the reference workload obligation and fitness trend (QLT-05)
body:
## What this does

QLT-05: a recipe can declare a reference workload and fitness functions; Deep contracts run it through the kernel; the kernel judges the report, keeps a series across contracts, and raises an attention item when a trend crosses its declared threshold.

- **Obligation.** A Deep contract in a project whose recipe record lists `workload` in `checks` owes `OB-workload` (kind `workload`, category `release`). Derived from the recipe record, not the file. Standard/Quick contracts and projects without `workload` owe none.
- **Declaration.** Strict `workload.json` v1 parsed in pure `core/fitness.ts`: `run` and optional `build` as argv arrays (shell and package-manager launchers refused), `report: "stdout"`, `timeoutMs`, `minimumSamples`, `samples`, up to 32 fitness functions with `measure`, `unit`, `better`, `target`, and `degradation` (`percent`, `consecutive` 2–12, `floor`) for trended ones. Invalid → receipt `inconclusive` with the new reason `workload-declaration-invalid`, nothing runs, the check does not abort.
- **Run.** Build and run argv are planned in the execution envelope (new command kind `workload`) and run through the existing runner, only after every other required obligation's process passed; otherwise the receipt is `skipped`.
- **Receipt.** The kernel judges the report against the declared targets (spec §5, recommendation "all A"): pass only for reference mode, enough samples, every target met, no harness reasons, exit 0. A missed target or an uncovered harness reason fails. Smoke/too few samples → `population-mismatch`; missing/invalid/contradictory reports and timeouts are inconclusive. Every workload receipt and check response carries the scope sentence (this concerns only the declared workload; the harness is project code; the kernel measures nothing).
- **Series and trend.** `finish` appends one point per function per contract to `project.fitness` (≤12) in the same publish that finishes the contract; a recorded receipt adds nothing. Each check applies the rule to stored points plus its own receipt: each of the last n points worse than the one before, and the change larger than max(percent of the first, floor). When it fires, the contract gets a `fitness-trend:` attention item and the verdict carries `fitness-trend-degraded` until the user or a reviewer disposes it (same-session does not clear it). After a raised window, the next one starts at its newest point. A changed environment tag restarts the comparison, and the response says so. The check response lists values as "the last n Deep contracts".

## Simplifications (disclosed, not built)

- The series tag uses platform, architecture, memory and node major **as the report states them**, not kernel observations (no `Runner.machine()`), so a report that misstates its environment is not caught (spec E6b not built).
- No `build-not-fresh` rule; report read from stdout only; no depth limit beyond the runner's 10 MB output bound; a failed build reads as `report-missing` with no wording of its own.
- `inspect why`, `finish` result text and the review manifest do not show the series. Only the check response and the verdict reason do.
- `workload.json` / `workload/*` are not added to any recipe's protected paths (WR-9 not built).
- No schema version bump or migration: `Receipt.workload`, `project.fitness` and the `workload` check value are optional additions, as trait results were.
- **The neutral starter is unchanged.** It ships no `workload/run.ts` harness, so it neither lists `workload` nor ships `workload.json`. QLT-05's "each application recipe shall declare" is therefore **not met for the starter** (spec Q4 option C, which narrows the requirement and is the owner's call).
- "Consecutive" means consecutive Deep contracts that ran the workload. That is narrower than the PRD's "consecutive checks" (spec Q2 A, not confirmed by the owner).
- Canonical specs (Tech Spec §§9.1, 12.7, App. C; UX wording) are not backfilled.
- The end-to-end test uses a **tiny fake harness** that prints a fixed-shape JSON report with a p95 the test sets. It measures nothing. Real wall time, the loan-desk harness and host behavior are unobserved.

## Tests

- `test/fitness.test.ts` `[QLT-05]` (pure, runs everywhere): strict declaration cases, obligation derivation, report judgement (pass, missed target, harness reason, smoke, too few samples, missing/invalid, contradictions), the trend rule (spec E8 values incl. zero base and higher-is-better), series idempotence, environment restart, the window after a raised item.
- `test/verdict.test.ts` `[QLT-05]`: the trend item holds the verdict below checked-local; same-session disposition does not clear it; user/reviewer does.
- `test/workload.test.ts` `[QLT-05]` (POSIX only; mutating work is refused on Windows): a Deep contract runs the fake harness and passes; a missed target fails; Standard and no-recipe contracts owe none; an invalid declaration is inconclusive without aborting; three consecutive Deep contracts at 100, 110, 121 ms raise one item, `inspect why` shows `fitness-trend-degraded`, a recheck adds no duplicate, a user disposition clears it, and finish records `raised`.

Local (Windows): typecheck, lint-arch, lint-skills, lint-quality, `npm run privacy` pass. `node tools/coverage.ts --milestone R1` lists QLT-05 as mapped; it still exits 1 for AGT-10, EVD-04, GIT-09 and CON-07, which other branches are building. The POSIX tests have not run locally. They first run in this PR's CI.
